evidence.claims: Checked: kit counts (pass), table values (pass, rounded correctly), 5 kg kit contents (pass), 'greedy never picks the mirrorless body' (pass), '160 Wh pack never chosen' (pass, tested), 'all device figures assumed' (honestly stated). Fails/partials: README:40 'the floor ... changes which kit wins at 2 and 4 kg' omits 3 kg (no floor 15/2.26 h, floor 12/16.47 h; indep.py confirms the winner changes at 2, 3 and 4 kg); headline README:3 'greedy stalls at 12 shots from 3 kg up' (it is already 12 at 2 kg, true but understated) and frames complementarity as defeating greedy, whereas a bundle-aware greedy (body+lens offered as one item, the textbook remedy) matches exact variety at every budget (scratchpad/capture/bundle.py: 12/15/18/18/18 at 2/3/4/5/7 kg); the limitation 'cameras are swapped between mounts' is stated for variety but the hours model assumes they all run at once, and this is not disclosed. 2.
evidence.fitness: Could a researcher build on it? The code is small and reusable, and capture-realkit already does (sourced devices). But the result is a known property: lens-needs-body is a precedence-constrained knapsack, and greedy failing on complementary items (variety = |bands| x |viewpoints| is supermodular, so the Nemhauser-Wolsey-Fisher 1978 greedy guarantee for submodular coverage does not apply) is textbook (Kellerer, Pferschy and Pisinger 2004, Knapsack Problems, precedence-constrained KP; Samphaiboon and Yamada 2000). None is cited; the greedy baseline is the naive one; catalogue is 15 assumed items. Not new, sound only within its assumed toy model, far from the research/CLAUDE.md PhD bar. 1.
evidence.domain: The battery rule matches FAA PackSafe: lithium-ion <= 100 Wh in carry-on without approval, 101-160 Wh with airline approval (the model correctly scopes to 'without approval' and checks internal batteries too). Departures a camera assistant would flag in the first hour: (1) internal inconsistency: variety assumes cameras move between mounts, hours divides carried Wh by the draw of one camera per mount running simultaneously (model.py:111); with one camera running at a time (consistent with the swap assumption) the 4 h floor never changes the winner (indep.py: floor-4h exact is 12/15/18 at 2/3/4 kg, identical to no-floor), so the README's 'the floor is not a detail' finding is an artefact of the inconsistency; (2) mount payload not modelled: a 150 g mini tripod, a selfie pole and a telescoping mast are each counted as holding a 1.55 kg body plus 70-200, which is what makes 18 shots reachable; with illustrative payload limits (pole 0.7, mini 0.8, mast 2.0 kg, my assumption) the 5 kg optimum is 14 shots; (3) Wh pooled across camera internals and USB packs at 100% efficiency; at a typical 80% power-bank delivery hours fall ~18% (16.76 -> 13.73 at 5 kg), variety unchanged. 2.

verdict: A small, clean, reproducible kit-packing study: run.py reproduces results.txt byte for byte in under a second, 10 tests pass, and an independent brute force reproduces all 16 table rows, the 17,280/11,520 kit counts and the 5 kg kit (4,970 g, 18 shots, 16.76 h). The numbers are right for the model; the conclusions drawn from it are weaker than stated. The hours model assumes every mounted camera runs at once while the variety model assumes cameras are swapped, and with a consistent one-at-a-time reading the 4 h floor never changes the winner. The headline greedy failure disappears when body+lens is offered as one item, the textbook remedy for precedence-constrained knapsack, and no prior work is cited. Mount payload is unmodelled, and 4 of 6 seeded mutants survive. Does not meet the bar (verification 2, claims 2, fitness 1).
